title: Drop order, step by step
subtitle: Live values on the stack and the output the program prints
noisyNote: Noisy(name) prints "drop name" when it is dropped

presets.label: Nested scopes
steps: a is created and owned by main's scope.
Entering a block opens a new scope. b is pushed on top of a.
c is declared after b, so it sits above it.
The block ends. Locals are dropped in reverse declaration order: c first…
…then b. Nothing from the inner scope survives the closing brace.
Back in main, d is declared after a.
main returns: d is dropped first, as the most recent local…
…and a last. The order is fully determined by the source code: no collector decides it.

presets.label: Struct fields
steps: x is a plain local.
p owns two fields. Fields are not separate locals: they live inside p.
At the end of main, p goes first (declared last). Its own Drop::drop runs before its fields, while they are still usable.
Then the fields are dropped in declaration order (not reverse!): first…
…then second. Now p is completely gone.
Finally x, the earliest local.

presets.label: Vec of items
steps: The Vec lives on the stack (pointer, length, capacity); its three elements live in a heap buffer it owns.
t is declared after v.
Reverse declaration order: t is dropped first.
Dropping a Vec drops its elements front to back: v0…
…v1…
…v2, and then the heap buffer itself is freed.

presets.label: Panic unwinding
steps: _m is a guard in main's frame.
main calls inner(): a new frame is pushed.
_g lives in inner's frame.
panic! runs the panic hook, which prints the message to stderr. Then unwinding starts.
Unwinding walks back up the call stack, running destructors frame by frame: _g first.
Then main's locals. Guards (locks, files, transactions) are released even on a panic. never printed is never reached.
The panic reached the top of the main thread: the process exits with code 101. With panic = "abort" none of these drops would run.
